name: Paul
title: Apostle to the Gentiles
tagline: Persecutor of the church, called on the road to Damascus.
story: Saul of Tarsus, a Pharisee who persecuted the church until the risen Jesus met him near Damascus; as Paul he carried the gospel to the Gentiles.

periods.title: The church in Acts
periods.sub: Three journeys, arrest, Rome; the letters

periods.title: After Scripture
periods.sub: Tradition, by who said it and when

entries.title: Born at Tarsus, brought up in Jerusalem
entries.text: Born a Jew in Tarsus in Cilicia, “a citizen of no mean city”, and “brought up in this city” (Jerusalem) “at the feet of Gamaliel”.

entries.title: A tentmaker
entries.text: A tentmaker, who worked with his own hands to keep himself and those with him.

entries.title: Of the tribe of Benjamin
entries.text: An Israelite of the tribe of Benjamin, “Circumcised the eighth day”, “an Hebrew of the Hebrews”.

entries.title: A Pharisee, son of a Pharisee
entries.text: “I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee.”

entries.title: A Roman citizen from birth
entries.text: A Roman citizen from birth: “But I was free born.”

entries.title: His sister’s son
entries.text: His sister's son in Jerusalem warned him of a plot to kill him.

entries.title: “My kinsmen”
entries.text: He calls Andronicus and Junia, Herodion, and Lucius, Jason and Sosipater “my kinsmen”.

entries.title: At Stephen’s stoning
entries.text: A “young man … whose name was Saul” kept the clothes of those who stoned Stephen, and “was consenting unto his death”.

entries.title: Making havock of the church
entries.text: He “made havock of the church”, putting men and women in prison, and asked the high priest for letters to bring believers bound from Damascus.

entries.title: Seen by the risen Lord “last of all”
Damascus, Arabia, the basket
entries.text: After his conversion he preached in the synagogues of Damascus, went into Arabia, came back to Damascus, and escaped over the wall in a basket.

entries.title: Fifteen days with Peter
entries.text: “After three years” he went up to Jerusalem to see Peter and stayed fifteen days; Barnabas brought him to the apostles. He was then sent to Tarsus and worked in “the regions of Syria and Cilicia”.

entries.title: A trance in the temple: “Depart: for I will send thee far hence unto the Gentiles”
A year at Antioch
entries.text: Barnabas brought him to Antioch, where they taught for a whole year, and the two carried famine relief to Jerusalem.

entries.title: The first journey
entries.text: First journey: sent out from Antioch with Barnabas to Cyprus and the cities of Pisidia and Lycaonia; at Lystra he was stoned and left for dead.

entries.title: The council at Jerusalem
entries.text: At the council in Jerusalem he and Barnabas told what God had done among the Gentiles.

entries.title: The second journey
entries.text: He parted from Barnabas over Mark and set out with Silas. Timothy joined them at Lystra; a vision called them to Macedonia; they went on to Philippi, Thessalonica, Berea and Athens, and he stayed eighteen months at Corinth.

entries.title: A vision at Corinth: “Be not afraid, but speak”
Three years at Ephesus
entries.text: Third journey: “by the space of three years” he worked from Ephesus, then went through Macedonia and Greece and said farewell to the Ephesian elders at Miletus.

entries.title: Seized, held, heard
entries.text: Seized in the temple at Jerusalem, he was held two years at Caesarea under Felix; before Festus he appealed to Caesar, and he spoke before King Agrippa.

entries.title: At night in Jerusalem: “so must thou bear witness also at Rome”
Shipwreck, and Rome
entries.text: On the voyage to Rome the ship was wrecked at Melita (Malta). At Rome he lived two whole years in his own hired house with a soldier guarding him, receiving all who came.

entries.title: His own list of sufferings
entries.text: His own list of sufferings: five times thirty-nine lashes, three beatings with rods, one stoning, three shipwrecks, “in prisons more frequent”.

entries.title: The prisons
entries.text: Prisons named in Scripture: Philippi, where he and Silas were put in the stocks; Herod's judgment hall at Caesarea; and Rome. In several letters he writes as a prisoner.

entries.title: Plans for Spain
entries.text: He planned to go on from Rome to Spain.

entries.title: Journeys in the letters
entries.text: The letters to Timothy and Titus name journeys that are hard to place in Acts: Timothy left at Ephesus when Paul went into Macedonia, Titus left in Crete, a winter planned at Nicopolis, a cloak left at Troas and Trophimus left sick at Miletum.

entries.title: Clement of Rome, 1 Clement 5:5-7
entries.text: Clement of Rome writes that Paul had been “seven times in bonds”, had “preached in the East and in the West”, reached “the farthest bounds of the West”, and when he had borne his testimony before the rulers “departed from the world”.

entries.title: Dionysius of Corinth, quoted by Eusebius, Church History 2.25.8
entries.text: Dionysius, bishop of Corinth, writes that Peter and Paul taught in Italy and “suffered martyrdom at the same time”.
entries.who: Dionysius of Corinth, quoted by Eusebius, Church History 2.25.8
entries.when: Dionysius about AD 170; Eusebius about AD 325

entries.title: The Muratorian fragment
entries.text: The Muratorian fragment says Luke's Acts leaves out “the journey of Paul, when he went from the city—Rome—to Spain”.

verses.text: And he fell to the earth, and heard a voice saying unto him, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?

cols.label: Acts 22: Paul to the crowd in Jerusalem

verses.text: And it came to pass, that, as I made my journey, and was come nigh unto Damascus about noon, suddenly there shone from heaven a great light round about me.

But rise, and stand upon thy feet: for I have appeared unto thee for this purpose, to make thee a minister and a witness both of these things which thou hast seen, and of those things in the which I will appear unto thee;
But when it pleased God, who separated me from my mother’s womb, and called me by his grace,
And when he had received meat, he was strengthened. Then was Saul certain days with the disciples which were at Damascus.
And straightway he preached Christ in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God.

But all that heard him were amazed, and said; Is not this he that destroyed them which called on this name in Jerusalem, and came hither for that intent, that he might bring them bound unto the chief priests?
But Saul increased the more in strength, and confounded the Jews which dwelt at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ.
¶ And after that many days were fulfilled, the Jews took counsel to kill him:
But their laying await was known of Saul. And they watched the gates day and night to kill him.
Then the disciples took him by night, and let him down by the wall in a basket.
Neither went I up to Jerusalem to them which were apostles before me; but I went into Arabia, and returned again unto Damascus.
In Damascus the governor under Aretas the king kept the city of the Damascenes with a garrison, desirous to apprehend me:
And through a window in a basket was I let down by the wall, and escaped his hands.
Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to see Peter, and abode with him fifteen days.
But other of the apostles saw I none, save James the Lord’s brother.
Now the things which I write unto you, behold, before God, I lie not.
Afterwards I came into the regions of Syria and Cilicia;
And when Saul was come to Jerusalem, he assayed to join himself to the disciples: but they were all afraid of him, and believed not that he was a disciple.

But Barnabas took him, and brought him to the apostles, and declared unto them how he had seen the Lord in the way, and that he had spoken to him, and how he had preached boldly at Damascus in the name of Jesus.
And he was with them coming in and going out at Jerusalem.
And he spake boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus, and disputed against the Grecians: but they went about to slay him.
Which when the brethren knew, they brought him down to Cæsarea, and sent him forth to Tarsus.
And certain men which came down from Judæa taught the brethren, and said, Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.

When therefore Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them, they determined that Paul and Barnabas, and certain other of them, should go up to Jerusalem unto the apostles and elders about this question.
And being brought on their way by the church, they passed through Phenice and Samaria, declaring the conversion of the Gentiles: and they caused great joy unto all the brethren.
And when they were come to Jerusalem, they were received of the church, and of the apostles and elders, and they declared all things that God had done with them.
But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.
¶ And the apostles and elders came together for to consider of this matter.

And when there had been much disputing, Peter rose up, and said unto them, Men and brethren, ye know how that a good while ago God made choice among us, that the Gentiles by my mouth should hear the word of the gospel, and believe.
And God, which knoweth the hearts, bare them witness, giving them the Holy Ghost, even as he did unto us;
And put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith.
Now therefore why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?
But we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they.
¶ Then all the multitude kept silence, and gave audience to Barnabas and Paul, declaring what miracles and wonders God had wrought among the Gentiles by them.
Then fourteen years after I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, and took Titus with me also.

And I went up by revelation, and communicated unto them that gospel which I preach among the Gentiles, but privately to them which were of reputation, lest by any means I should run, or had run, in vain.
But neither Titus, who was with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised:
And that because of false brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage:
To whom we gave place by subjection, no, not for an hour; that the truth of the gospel might continue with you.
But of these who seemed to be somewhat, (whatsoever they were, it maketh no matter to me: God accepteth no man’s person:) for they who seemed to be somewhat in conference added nothing to me:
But contrariwise, when they saw that the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter;
(For he that wrought effectually in Peter to the apostleship of the circumcision, the same was mighty in me toward the Gentiles:)

And when James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars, perceived the grace that was given unto me, they gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship; that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision.
Only they would that we should remember the poor; the same which I also was forward to do.

items.q: Did the men with Saul hear the voice? Acts 9:7 says they were “hearing a voice”; Acts 22:9 that “they heard not the voice of him that spake to me”.
items.full: Did the men with Saul hear the voice? Acts 9:7 says they were “hearing a voice”; Acts 22:9 that “they heard not the voice of him that spake to me”. (In date order.)
items.from: This page

views.label: They heard a sound, not the words
views.holders: Matthew Henry (early 18th century); W. J. Conybeare and J. S. Howson (1891), who also report Wordsworth and Hackett

argument.text: Henry: they heard “a confused noise” but did not understand what was said. Conybeare and Howson: the voice spoke articulately to Saul, but to the rest it was “a sound mysterious and indistinct”.

views.label: Leave the differences as they stand
views.holders: W. J. Conybeare and J. S. Howson (1891)

argument.text: They judge it “both more prudent and more honest to leave these well-known discrepancies exactly as they are found in the Bible”, and note that readers explain them differently according to their view of inspiration.

items.q: Was Paul released after Acts 28 and imprisoned again?
items.full: Was Paul released after Acts 28 and imprisoned again? (Most widely held view in these sources first.)
items.from: This page

views.label: Released, travelled, re-arrested, executed
views.holders: Eusebius (about AD 325); Conybeare and Howson (1891); Schaff (1890), who is “disposed to admit” it; Rutherfurd, ISBE (1915)

argument.text: Clement's “farthest bounds of the West”, the Muratorian fragment's journey to Spain, Paul's own plan to visit Spain, and the journeys in the letters to Timothy and Titus that Acts has no room for.

views.label: No release: he died at the end of the Roman custody
views.holders: Wieseler and Schrader, as reported and answered by Conybeare and Howson (1891)

argument.text: Acts and the other early sources are silent about later travel, and “the farthest bounds of the West” may mean Rome itself.

views.label: The letters to Timothy and Titus are not Paul's, so they prove nothing either way
views.holders: F. C. Baur and others, as reported by Schaff (1890) and Rutherfurd (ISBE, 1915)

argument.text: On this view the journeys those letters mention are no evidence for a release.

items.q: When did these things happen? Scripture gives no years; two public-domain reckonings, side by side.
items.full: When did these things happen? Scripture gives no years; two public-domain reckonings, side by side. (Older first.)

views.label: Ramsay (1895)
views.holders: W. M. Ramsay, St. Paul the Traveller, Chronological Index

argument.text: Conversion AD 33; first journey from spring 47 to August 49; council winter 49-50; arrival in Jerusalem at Pentecost 57; Rome to the end of 61; second trial 67.

views.label: Robertson (1915)
views.holders: A. T. Robertson, ISBE, “Paul, the Apostle”, part 3

argument.text: Stephen's death, and so the conversion, about 35; first journey 47-48 (or 48-49); council 49 (or 50); arrest spring 57; reaches Rome early in 60; released 63 or early 64; death by early summer 68, possibly 67. Robertson warns: “There is not a single date in the life of Paul that is beyond dispute, though several are narrowed to a fine point.”

items.q: Did Paul write Ephesians, Colossians and the pastoral letters?
items.full: Did Paul write Ephesians, Colossians and the pastoral letters?
items.from: Asked on the Paul's letters page

views.label: All by Paul
views.holders: The ancient church (Eusebius: Paul's letters "well known and undisputed"); for Ephesians and Colossians Bleek, Meyer, B. Weiss, Alford and Farrar; for the pastoral letters Huther, Wiesinger, Wieseler, Lange, Alford, Farrar, Salmon, B. Weiss and others (as listed by Schaff and ISBE)

argument.text: Each letter names Paul in its first verse, and ancient writers accepted all of them. Marcion did reject the pastoral letters, which, Tertullian notes, "all treat of ecclesiastical discipline". Schaff answers the vocabulary argument by noting that Romans, the Corinthian letters, Galatians and Philippians also have many words found nowhere else in the New Testament.

views.label: Ephesians or Colossians not by Paul
views.holders: De Wette (Ephesians "a verbose expansion" of Colossians); Renan and Ewald (kept Colossians, gave up Ephesians); Mayerhoff (Colossians an abridgment of Ephesians); Baur, Schwegler and Hilgenfeld (both, from a later anti-Gnostic writer); Holtzmann, Pfleiderer and others

argument.text: The two letters overlap so closely that critics have argued one is a later writer's reworking of the other, or both of something earlier. ISBE concludes instead for "simultaneous authorship by one writer".

views.label: The pastoral letters not by Paul
views.holders: J. E. C. Schmidt and Schleiermacher (1 Timothy); Baur, who dated them about 150; Holtzmann, whose 1880 work made the fullest case from their vocabulary; Renan, Pfleiderer, Ewald, Hausrath and others

argument.text: Holtzmann made the fullest case from their language: Schaff, citing him, counts 169 of their words found nowhere else in the New Testament. Baur dated them about 150, and Pfleiderer placed 2 Timothy under Trajan and the other two under Hadrian. Renan thought a forger had worked in a few genuine notes of Paul's.

items.q: Was Paul released after the two years in Rome, and imprisoned a second time?
items.full: Was Paul released after the two years in Rome, and imprisoned a second time?
items.from: Asked on the Paul's letters page

views.label: Released, travelled, arrested again and executed
views.holders: Eusebius; Conybeare and Howson, adding Chrysostom and Jerome; ISBE; Easton; Schaff ("disposed to admit" it)

argument.text: The pastoral letters mention journeys that do not fit Acts: Timothy left at Ephesus, Titus in Crete, a winter at Nicopolis, a cloak at Troas. Clement of Rome says Paul reached "the farthest bounds of the West"; the Muratorian fragment speaks of a journey from Rome to Spain; and Eusebius reports that Paul was sent out again to preach and martyred on a second visit to Rome, citing 2 Timothy's "first answer".

views.label: Not released
views.holders: Wieseler and Schrader (as criticised by Conybeare and Howson)

argument.text: Acts and the other early sources are silent about later travel, and Clement's "extremity of the West" (Conybeare and Howson's rendering) may simply mean Rome: Wieseler translated the words as the sovereign of Rome, and Schrader argued they cannot mean Spain because Paul was not martyred there.

views.label: Pastoral letters written during the Acts period
views.holders: One proposal reported by Schaff

argument.text: The journeys could be unrecorded trips during Paul's three years at Ephesus, about 56-57.

views.label: No evidence either way
views.holders: Those who deny that Paul wrote the pastoral letters

argument.text: If the pastoral letters are not Paul's, their travel notes say nothing about his last years.

items.q: Where was Paul held when he wrote the prison letters: Rome, Caesarea or Ephesus?
items.full: Where was Paul held when he wrote the prison letters: Rome, Caesarea or Ephesus?
items.from: Asked on the Paul's letters page

views.label: Rome
views.holders: The oldest tradition and "most modern writers" (Lightfoot); Conybeare and Howson; the ISBE articles; Easton

argument.text: Acts ends with two years in Rome, in a rented house under guard, receiving all who came. Greetings from "Caesar's household" fit Rome; Lightfoot held they could not fairly fit Caesarea, and that at Caesarea, having appealed to Caesar, Paul had no reason to expect release and a visit to Macedonia.

views.label: Caesarea
views.holders: Böttger, Thiersch, Reuss and H. A. W. Meyer for Ephesians, Colossians and Philemon; H. E. G. Paulus, Böttger and Thiersch for Philippians (reported by Lightfoot)

argument.text: Paul was also held two years at Caesarea under Felix, with friends free to visit, and the "palace" of Philippians 1:13 is the same Greek word used for Herod's judgment hall there.

views.label: Ephesus
views.holders: The Latin prologue to Colossians in Codex Fuldensis; Deissmann, Lisco, Albertz and Bacon, "a growing opinion" in 1915 (as reported by Robertson, ISBE)

argument.text: Paul's own record mentions prisons "more frequent" than Acts reports, a fight with beasts at Ephesus and deadly trouble in Asia, and Clement of Rome says he was in bonds seven times.

items.q: Did Paul write 2 Thessalonians, and which of the two letters came first?
items.full: Did Paul write 2 Thessalonians, and which of the two letters came first?
items.from: Asked on the Paul's letters page

views.label: Not by Paul
views.holders: Baur (who, Schaff reports, regarded the first letter as an imitation of the second); Hilgenfeld, who dated it to Trajan's reign as "a sort of Pauline Apocalypse" (reported by Schaff)

argument.text: Its teaching on the Lord's coming seems to differ from the first letter ("In the First Letter he coaxes; in the Second Letter he commands", as Walker summarises the case), its tone is cooler, and its "man of sin" is unlike anything else in Paul.

views.label: By Paul
views.holders: Walker (ISBE); Harnack, who thought it was addressed to a Jewish-Christian group in the church

argument.text: Jesus' own teaching, Walker notes, holds together the call to "watch, for in such an hour as they think not the Son of man cometh" and the warning that "the end is not yet"; and a sterner second note is natural if the gentler first one had not worked. Walker saw scholars of every camp returning to the traditional view.

views.label: Written before 1 Thessalonians
views.holders: Grotius and Ewald, who held both letters genuine (reported by Schaff)

argument.text: The order of the two letters in the Bible is not necessarily the order in which they were written.

items.q: How many letters did Paul write to Corinth, and which was the letter written "with many tears"?
items.full: How many letters did Paul write to Corinth, and which was the letter written "with many tears"?
items.from: Asked on the Paul's letters page

views.label: Four letters, two of them lost
views.holders: Read from the letters themselves

argument.text: The two surviving letters point to at least four: a lost earlier letter about not keeping company with fornicators, 1 Corinthians, a letter written "out of much affliction and anguish of heart", and 2 Corinthians. Shaw (ISBE) suggests that 2 Corinthians 6:14-7:1 may preserve a stray piece of the lost first letter.

views.label: The tearful letter is 1 Corinthians
views.holders: Easton

argument.text: Easton applies Paul's description of anguish and tears to 1 Corinthians itself. He also doubts any unrecorded painful visit, reading "the third time I am ready to come" as an intention only.

views.label: A separate letter, now lost
views.holders: Shaw (ISBE)

argument.text: Shaw treats "the severe letter" as a letter of its own, written after a painful second visit that Acts does not record.

views.label: The tearful letter survives as 2 Corinthians 10-13
views.holders: Hausrath (1870), followed by Schmiedel, Pfleiderer, Lipsius, Clemen, von Soden, McGiffert, Plummer, Moffatt, Peake, J. H. Kennedy and others (as listed by Shaw, ISBE)

argument.text: Everyone agrees on a remarkable change of tone at chapter 10. On this view the last four chapters are part of the painful letter, later joined to the gentler one.

views.label: 2 Corinthians is one letter
views.holders: Sanday, A. Robertson, Holtzmann, Beyschlag, Weizsäcker, Sabatier, Godet, Bernard, Denney, Weiss and Zahn (as listed by Shaw, ISBE)

argument.text: The change of tone is real, but it does not prove that two letters were joined; A. Robertson called the case "decidedly not proven".

items.q: Was the last chapter of Romans, with its long list of greetings, written to Rome?
items.full: Was the last chapter of Romans, with its long list of greetings, written to Rome?
items.from: Asked on the Paul's letters page

views.label: A note to Ephesus attached later
views.holders: Reuss, Ewald and Farrar (named by Schaff); others reported by Moule (ISBE)

argument.text: Paul greets so many people in a city he had never visited that some thought the greetings, Romans 16:1-15 or 16:3-20, belonged to a separate note sent to Ephesus.

views.label: One circular letter with several endings
views.holders: Renan

argument.text: Renan guessed that an editor had combined four copies of a single circular letter, each with a different ending.

views.label: Chapters 15-16 not genuine
views.holders: Baur

argument.text: Baur rejected the last two chapters altogether; Hilgenfeld and Pfleiderer defended them against him.

views.label: Part of the letter to Rome
views.holders: Hort, A. Robertson, Hilgenfeld, Pfleiderer (reported by Moule and Schaff)

argument.text: Of some 300 manuscripts of Romans, Moule reports, not one that is undamaged lacks the complete letter. The doubts in the manuscripts concern the closing doxology, which some copies place after chapter 14 and three, with Marcion, leave out.

items.q: Was "Ephesians" written to Ephesus? The words "at Ephesus" are missing from the oldest manuscripts.
items.full: Was "Ephesians" written to Ephesus? The words "at Ephesus" are missing from the oldest manuscripts.
items.from: Asked on the Paul's letters page

views.label: To Ephesus
views.holders: Tertullian, appealing to "the true tradition of the Church"

argument.text: The Textus Receptus and the KJV read "at Ephesus", and the church received the letter under that title.

views.label: To Laodicea
views.holders: Marcion

argument.text: Marcion's collection called it the letter "to the Laodiceans".

views.label: A circular letter for the churches of Asia
views.holders: Archbishop Ussher, who first proposed it; Lightfoot, Conybeare and Howson, Lewis (ISBE), Easton

argument.text: Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus lack "at Ephesus"; Origen knew nothing of the words and Basil reported old copies without them. The letter has no personal greetings, though Paul spent three years at Ephesus, and speaks as if some readers had only heard of him. On this view the copy that reached Laodicea is "the epistle from Laodicea" of Colossians 4:16.

items.q: Who were "the churches of Galatia": the old Celtic territory in the north, or the southern cities of the Roman province?
items.full: Who were "the churches of Galatia": the old Celtic territory in the north, or the southern cities of the Roman province?
items.from: Asked on the Paul's letters page

views.label: North Galatia
views.holders: Earlier scholars up to Lightfoot and Salmon; later Chase, Dods, Sabatier, Harnack, H. Holtzmann, Jülicher, Lipsius, Mommsen, Schmiedel, Schürer and others; Findlay himself (as listed by Findlay, ISBE)

argument.text: The letter went to churches in old Galatia around Ancyra, Pessinus and Tavium, which Paul first reached on his second journey when he passed through "the region of Galatia". On this view the letter is later rather than earlier. Robertson judged in 1915 that it "still has the weight of authority".

views.label: South Galatia
views.holders: First proposed by Mynster (1825); then Perrot, Renan, Pfleiderer, Weizsäcker, Ramsay, von Soden, Bartlet, Gifford, Rendall, Sanday ("with hesitation") and others (as listed by Findlay, ISBE)

argument.text: The letter went to Pisidian Antioch, Iconium, Lystra and Derbe, the churches Paul founded on his first journey, all inside the Roman province of Galatia. Ramsay's books made this view widely known from 1895, and some of its supporters make Galatians the earliest of Paul's letters.

items.q: Who wrote Hebrews?
items.from: Asked on the Hebrews page

views.label: Paul
views.holders: Pantaenus and Clement of Alexandria (late 2nd century); the Eastern churches; Athanasius (367); later the Latin West through Jerome and Augustine and the councils of Hippo (393) and Carthage (419); in modern times Ebrard, Hofmann, Biesenthal, Kay and Easton's Bible Dictionary (1897).

argument.text: For: Timothy is mentioned (13:23), and Origen judged the thoughts to be the apostle's. Pantaenus explained the missing name: Paul, sent to the Gentiles, would not call himself apostle to the Hebrews. Clement added that Paul did not want to put off readers who distrusted him. The KJV's "me in my bonds" (10:34) seemed to point to Paul the prisoner, though Westcott's Greek text reads "the prisoners". Against: Paul says he received his gospel from no man, but this writer learned it from others (2:3), a point Westcott calls grave, even fatal. Origen found the Greek purer than Paul's, the writer always quotes the Greek Old Testament, and the church at Rome long disputed the claim.

views.label: Barnabas
views.holders: Tertullian (about AD 220); revived by Cameron in the 17th century; later Ritschl, Weiss, Renan, Salmon, Grau and Zahn (as listed by Dods and Westcott).

argument.text: For: it is the only named tradition besides Paul. Barnabas was a Levite, which would suit a writer so absorbed in priesthood. His nickname, "son of consolation", uses the same Greek word as the writer's "word of exhortation" (13:22). He was a Greek-speaking Cypriot in Paul's circle. Against: the tradition is found only in North Africa, and Origen does not know it. Dods and Rees treat the word match as coincidence. Davidson thinks his early story hardly fits 2:3.

views.label: Luke
views.holders: Clement of Alexandria (as translator of a letter Paul wrote in Hebrew); reported by Origen; Calvin (Luke or Clement); Delitzsch.

argument.text: For: ancient readers noticed that the style is like that of Acts, a likeness Westcott calls remarkable. Against: it may only mean the writer knew Luke's work or circle. If the letter was never translated from Hebrew, the main reason for naming Luke largely falls away. The Alexandrian cast of the letter's thought is not found in Luke.

views.label: Clement of Rome
views.holders: Reported by Origen; Eusebius (as the likelier translator); mentioned by Calvin.

argument.text: For: Clement's letter to Corinth (about AD 96) borrows heavily from Hebrews; its chapter 36 reworks Heb 1:3–4 and the psalms of 1:5–13. Jerome also noticed the likeness. Against: Westcott reads the parallels as Clement using Hebrews, just as he uses Paul's letters. Clement combines but does not create, and the depth of thought is far apart.

views.label: Apollos
views.holders: First suggested by Martin Luther (as reported by Westcott and Dods); then Bleek, Tholuck, Hilgenfeld, Lünemann, Reuss, Pfleiderer, Alford, Farrar, Plumptre and Kurtz; Bartlet in the 1911 Britannica, writing to Asia.

argument.text: For: Acts describes him as an Alexandrian Jew, "an eloquent man, and mighty in the scriptures", who showed from the scriptures that Jesus was the Christ. He belonged to Paul's circle. Davidson felt no better words could describe the writer of Hebrews. Against: no ancient writer suggests him. Westcott notes there is no evidence that Apollos wrote anything, and sees the guess as a reluctance to admit we do not know.

views.label: Priscilla (and Aquila)
views.holders: Adolf Harnack (1900, as reported by Dods and Rees); Bleek had almost argued for Aquila; Rendel Harris was sympathetic.

argument.text: For: the couple taught Apollos, worked with Paul, knew Timothy and hosted a church in their home at Rome. Harnack read the change between "I" and "we" as a sign of two writers, and argued that the name was dropped because of prejudice against a woman teaching. Against: the writer speaks of himself as one man (11:32; 13:19, 22–23) and seems to be one of the leaders, as Dods points out; Rees answers Harnack that Paul too moves between "I" and "we", in Romans for one, where no one suggests two writers.

views.label: Silas (Silvanus)
views.holders: Named as possible by Westcott; listed by Easton and in the ISBE.

argument.text: For: Silas belonged to Paul's circle, and 1 Peter was written "by Silvanus". Against: Westcott says only that the idea is consistent with what we know of him.

views.label: Others
views.holders: Mark (E. S. Lowndes, as reported by Westcott); Philip the deacon and Aristion (listed in the ISBE).

argument.text: Mostly guesswork. Rees calls these names little more than names to us. Jesus' own disciples are ruled out, because the writer heard the gospel second-hand (2:3).

views.label: Unknown
views.holders: Origen; Dods (1910), who thought it best to confess our ignorance; Rees in the ISBE (1915).

argument.text: Origen said that only God knows who wrote the letter. Dods preferred to admit ignorance, though he thought Aquila fitted a Roman destination as well as anyone. Rees leaned toward someone like Apollos but left the answer with God.

items.q: Which letter was written first?
items.from: Asked on the The letters of the New Testament page

views.label: James
views.holders: Philip Schaff (1890); J. B. Mayor (1892) dated it to the 40s

argument.text: Schaff placed James "before A.D. 50" and called it "probably the oldest of the New Testament books"; it "takes no notice of the circumcision controversy" that fills Galatians.

views.label: Galatians
views.holders: John Calvin (1548); some holders of the South Galatian view (reported by Robertson, ISBE)

argument.text: Calvin thought Galatians was written "before that consultation had been held" in Acts 15, since Paul would surely have cited the council's decree; Robertson reports that some South Galatian scholars make it "the very earliest of Paul's Epistles".

views.label: 1 Thessalonians
views.holders: M. G. Easton (1897); George Milligan (1908, reported by Robertson, ISBE)

argument.text: Written from Corinth soon after Timothy returned from Thessalonica: "the first of all Paul's epistles" (Easton).

items.q: Which visit to Jerusalem took Titus with Paul (Galatians 2:1)?
items.full: Which visit to Jerusalem took Titus with Paul (Galatians 2:1)? (Older view first.)
items.from: Asked on Titus’s page

views.label: The council of Acts 15
views.holders: Irenaeus (about 180); Lightfoot (1890); Smith (1884); Rutherfurd, ISBE (1915)

argument.text: Lightfoot: the visit “has from the earliest times been identified with the visit recorded in Acts xv”: the same places, people and question. Rutherfurd counts Titus among “certain other of them” in Acts 15:2.

views.label: The famine-relief visit of Acts 11:30
views.holders: Ramsay (1895)

argument.text: Ramsay takes Titus to have been an assistant on the relief journey, and argues Paul would not have brought “an uncircumcised Greek” to the council itself.

items.q: Was Titus circumcised at Jerusalem (Galatians 2:3–5)?
items.full: Was Titus circumcised at Jerusalem (Galatians 2:3–5)? (Most widely held view first.)
items.from: Asked on Titus’s page

views.label: No: Paul did not yield
views.holders: Lightfoot (1890), with “the vast majority of early writers”; Rutherfurd, ISBE (1915)

argument.text: Lightfoot: the incident is told to show Paul never conceded circumcision, and Paul “could scarcely say ‘we yielded no not for an hour’ in the same breath” as confessing it.

views.label: Yes: he was circumcised, but not by compulsion
views.holders: Farrar (1879); Pelagius, the one early exception Lightfoot found; “several modern critics” (Lightfoot)

argument.text: Farrar asks why Paul's sentence is “so ambiguous, so involved” if he did not yield, and reads “was compelled” to mean Titus was circumcised “but not under compulsion”.

items.q: Who made the vow at Cenchrea (Acts 18:18)?
items.full: Who made the vow at Cenchrea (Acts 18:18)? (Order: as in these sources.)
items.from: Asked on Priscilla and Aquila’s page

views.label: Aquila
views.holders: Conybeare and Howson (1891), in their text, “left as it stood in the earlier editions”

argument.text: They describe Aquila ending a Jewish vow before sailing; their own note admits that “the arguments from the structure of the original are rather in favour of referring the vow, not to Aquila, but to St. Paul”.

views.label: Paul
views.holders: Ramsay (1895)

argument.text: Ramsay: “Though the grammatical construction of v. 18 would suggest that Aquila made the vow … the natural emphasis marks Paul as the subject here.”

items.q: Why did John Mark turn back at Perga?
items.full: Why did John Mark turn back at Perga? (Scripture does not say; views in the order they were published.)
items.from: Asked on John Mark’s page

views.label: He did not like the work, or wanted to see his mother
views.holders: Matthew Henry (1706-1721)

argument.text: Henry offers both reasons as guesses and adds that Mark left “without the consent of Paul and Barnabas”.

views.label: No reason can be known
views.holders: Smith (1884: “for some unexplained reason”); Fenlon (Catholic Encyclopedia, 1907: Luke “does not state”)

argument.text: Acts gives only Paul's later complaint that Mark “went not with them to the work”.

views.label: He shrank from the toil
views.holders: MacRory (1910), who says Acts 15:38 “seems to suggest that he feared the toil”

argument.text: The journey after Perga led inland to Antioch in Pisidia, Iconium and Lystra.

views.label: He objected to offering salvation to Gentiles on faith alone
views.holders: J. H. Farmer (ISBE, 1915)

argument.text: Farmer points to the conversion of Sergius Paulus at Paphos just before, where Paul takes the lead, and to Paul's strong words in Acts 15:38.

verses.44009021: But all that heard him were amazed, and said; Is not this he that destroyed them which called on this name in Jerusalem, and came hither for that intent, that he might bring them bound unto the chief priests?
verses.44009022: But Saul increased the more in strength, and confounded the Jews which dwelt at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ.
verses.44009023: ¶ And after that many days were fulfilled, the Jews took counsel to kill him:
verses.44009024: But their laying await was known of Saul. And they watched the gates day and night to kill him.
verses.44009025: Then the disciples took him by night, and let him down by the wall in a basket.
verses.44009026: And when Saul was come to Jerusalem, he assayed to join himself to the disciples: but they were all afraid of him, and believed not that he was a disciple.
verses.44009027: But Barnabas took him, and brought him to the apostles, and declared unto them how he had seen the Lord in the way, and that he had spoken to him, and how he had preached boldly at Damascus in the name of Jesus.
verses.44009028: And he was with them coming in and going out at Jerusalem.
verses.44009029: And he spake boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus, and disputed against the Grecians: but they went about to slay him.
verses.44009030: Which when the brethren knew, they brought him down to Cæsarea, and sent him forth to Tarsus.
verses.44011025: Then departed Barnabas to Tarsus, for to seek Saul:
verses.44011026: And when he had found him, he brought him unto Antioch. And it came to pass, that a whole year they assembled themselves with the church, and taught much people. And the disciples were called Christians first in Antioch.
verses.44011027: ¶ And in these days came prophets from Jerusalem unto Antioch.
verses.44011028: And there stood up one of them named Agabus, and signified by the Spirit that there should be great dearth throughout all the world: which came to pass in the days of Claudius Cæsar.
verses.44011029: Then the disciples, every man according to his ability, determined to send relief unto the brethren which dwelt in Judæa:
verses.44011030: Which also they did, and sent it to the elders by the hands of Barnabas and Saul.
verses.44012025: And Barnabas and Saul returned from Jerusalem, when they had fulfilled their ministry, and took with them John, whose surname was Mark.
verses.44013001: Now there were in the church that was at Antioch certain prophets and teachers; as Barnabas, and Simeon that was called Niger, and Lucius of Cyrene, and Manaen, which had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.
verses.44013002: As they ministered to the Lord, and fasted, the Holy Ghost said, Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them.
verses.44013003: And when they had fasted and prayed, and laid their hands on them, they sent them away.
verses.44013004: ¶ So they, being sent forth by the Holy Ghost, departed unto Seleucia; and from thence they sailed to Cyprus.
verses.44013005: And when they were at Salamis, they preached the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews: and they had also John to their minister.
verses.44013006: And when they had gone through the isle unto Paphos, they found a certain sorcerer, a false prophet, a Jew, whose name was Bar-jesus:
verses.44013007: Which was with the deputy of the country, Sergius Paulus, a prudent man; who called for Barnabas and Saul, and desired to hear the word of God.
verses.44013008: But Elymas the sorcerer (for so is his name by interpretation) withstood them, seeking to turn away the deputy from the faith.
verses.44013009: Then Saul, (who also is called Paul,) filled with the Holy Ghost, set his eyes on him,
verses.44013010: And said, O full of all subtilty and all mischief, thou child of the devil, thou enemy of all righteousness, wilt thou not cease to pervert the right ways of the Lord?
verses.44013011: And now, behold, the hand of the Lord is upon thee, and thou shalt be blind, not seeing the sun for a season. And immediately there fell on him a mist and a darkness; and he went about seeking some to lead him by the hand.
verses.44013012: Then the deputy, when he saw what was done, believed, being astonished at the doctrine of the Lord.
verses.44013013: Now when Paul and his company loosed from Paphos, they came to Perga in Pamphylia: and John departing from them returned to Jerusalem.
verses.44013014: ¶ But when they departed from Perga, they came to Antioch in Pisidia, and went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and sat down.
verses.44014001: And it came to pass in Iconium, that they went both together into the synagogue of the Jews, and so spake, that a great multitude both of the Jews and also of the Greeks believed.
verses.44014008: ¶ And there sat a certain man at Lystra, impotent in his feet, being a cripple from his mother’s womb, who never had walked:
verses.44014009: The same heard Paul speak: who stedfastly beholding him, and perceiving that he had faith to be healed,
verses.44014019: ¶ And there came thither certain Jews from Antioch and Iconium, who persuaded the people, and, having stoned Paul, drew him out of the city, supposing he had been dead.
verses.44014020: Howbeit, as the disciples stood round about him, he rose up, and came into the city: and the next day he departed with Barnabas to Derbe.
verses.44014026: And thence sailed to Antioch, from whence they had been recommended to the grace of God for the work which they fulfilled.
verses.44015001: And certain men which came down from Judæa taught the brethren, and said, Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.
verses.44015002: When therefore Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them, they determined that Paul and Barnabas, and certain other of them, should go up to Jerusalem unto the apostles and elders about this question.
verses.44015003: And being brought on their way by the church, they passed through Phenice and Samaria, declaring the conversion of the Gentiles: and they caused great joy unto all the brethren.
verses.44015004: And when they were come to Jerusalem, they were received of the church, and of the apostles and elders, and they declared all things that God had done with them.
verses.44015005: But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.
verses.44015006: ¶ And the apostles and elders came together for to consider of this matter.
verses.44015007: And when there had been much disputing, Peter rose up, and said unto them, Men and brethren, ye know how that a good while ago God made choice among us, that the Gentiles by my mouth should hear the word of the gospel, and believe.
verses.44015008: And God, which knoweth the hearts, bare them witness, giving them the Holy Ghost, even as he did unto us;
verses.44015009: And put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith.
verses.44015010: Now therefore why tempt ye God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples, which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?
verses.44015011: But we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they.
verses.44015012: ¶ Then all the multitude kept silence, and gave audience to Barnabas and Paul, declaring what miracles and wonders God had wrought among the Gentiles by them.
verses.44015013: ¶ And after they had held their peace, James answered, saying, Men and brethren, hearken unto me:
verses.44015014: Simeon hath declared how God at the first did visit the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for his name.
verses.44015022: Then pleased it the apostles and elders, with the whole church, to send chosen men of their own company to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas; namely, Judas surnamed Barsabas, and Silas, chief men among the brethren:
verses.44015027: We have sent therefore Judas and Silas, who shall also tell you the same things by mouth.
verses.44015032: And Judas and Silas, being prophets also themselves, exhorted the brethren with many words, and confirmed them.
verses.44015036: ¶ And some days after Paul said unto Barnabas, Let us go again and visit our brethren in every city where we have preached the word of the Lord, and see how they do.
verses.44015037: And Barnabas determined to take with them John, whose surname was Mark.
verses.44015038: But Paul thought not good to take him with them, who departed from them from Pamphylia, and went not with them to the work.
verses.44015039: And the contention was so sharp between them, that they departed asunder one from the other: and so Barnabas took Mark, and sailed unto Cyprus;
verses.44015040: And Paul chose Silas, and departed, being recommended by the brethren unto the grace of God.
verses.44015041: And he went through Syria and Cilicia, confirming the churches.
verses.44016001: Then came he to Derbe and Lystra: and, behold, a certain disciple was there, named Timotheus, the son of a certain woman, which was a Jewess, and believed; but his father was a Greek:
verses.44016002: Which was well reported of by the brethren that were at Lystra and Iconium.
verses.44016003: Him would Paul have to go forth with him; and took and circumcised him because of the Jews which were in those quarters: for they knew all that his father was a Greek.
verses.44016004: And as they went through the cities, they delivered them the decrees for to keep, that were ordained of the apostles and elders which were at Jerusalem.
verses.44016005: And so were the churches established in the faith, and increased in number daily.
verses.44016006: Now when they had gone throughout Phrygia and the region of Galatia, and were forbidden of the Holy Ghost to preach the word in Asia,
verses.44016008: And they passing by Mysia came down to Troas.
verses.44016012: And from thence to Philippi, which is the chief city of that part of Macedonia, and a colony: and we were in that city abiding certain days.
verses.44016014: ¶ And a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, which worshipped God, heard us: whose heart the Lord opened, that she attended unto the things which were spoken of Paul.
verses.44016019: ¶ And when her masters saw that the hope of their gains was gone, they caught Paul and Silas, and drew them into the marketplace unto the rulers,
verses.44016023: And when they had laid many stripes upon them, they cast them into prison, charging the jailor to keep them safely:
verses.44016024: Who, having received such a charge, thrust them into the inner prison, and made their feet fast in the stocks.
verses.44016025: ¶ And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them.
verses.44016037: But Paul said unto them, They have beaten us openly uncondemned, being Romans, and have cast us into prison; and now do they thrust us out privily? nay verily; but let them come themselves and fetch us out.
verses.44016040: And they went out of the prison, and entered into the house of Lydia: and when they had seen the brethren, they comforted them, and departed.
verses.44017001: Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where was a synagogue of the Jews:
verses.44017002: And Paul, as his manner was, went in unto them, and three sabbath days reasoned with them out of the scriptures,
verses.44017010: ¶ And the brethren immediately sent away Paul and Silas by night unto Berea: who coming thither went into the synagogue of the Jews.
verses.44017014: And then immediately the brethren sent away Paul to go as it were to the sea: but Silas and Timotheus abode there still.
verses.44017015: And they that conducted Paul brought him unto Athens: and receiving a commandment unto Silas and Timotheus for to come to him with all speed, they departed.
verses.44017022: ¶ Then Paul stood in the midst of Mars’ hill, and said, Ye men of Athens, I perceive that in all things ye are too superstitious.
verses.44018001: After these things Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth;
verses.44018002: And found a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla; (because that Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome:) and came unto them.
verses.44018003: And because he was of the same craft, he abode with them, and wrought: for by their occupation they were tentmakers.
verses.44018009: Then spake the Lord to Paul in the night by a vision, Be not afraid, but speak, and hold not thy peace:
verses.44018010: For I am with thee, and no man shall set on thee to hurt thee: for I have much people in this city.
verses.44018011: And he continued there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.
verses.44018018: ¶ And Paul after this tarried there yet a good while, and then took his leave of the brethren, and sailed thence into Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila; having shorn his head in Cenchrea: for he had a vow.
verses.44018023: And after he had spent some time there, he departed, and went over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.
verses.44018024: ¶ And a certain Jew named Apollos, born at Alexandria, an eloquent man, and mighty in the scriptures, came to Ephesus.
verses.44018025: This man was instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in the spirit, he spake and taught diligently the things of the Lord, knowing only the baptism of John.
verses.44018026: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue: whom when Aquila and Priscilla had heard, they took him unto them, and expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly.
verses.44018027: And when he was disposed to pass into Achaia, the brethren wrote, exhorting the disciples to receive him: who, when he was come, helped them much which had believed through grace:
verses.44018028: For he mightily convinced the Jews, and that publickly, shewing by the scriptures that Jesus was Christ.
verses.44019001: And it came to pass, that, while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul having passed through the upper coasts came to Ephesus: and finding certain disciples,
verses.44019002: He said unto them, Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed? And they said unto him, We have not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost.
verses.44019003: And he said unto them, Unto what then were ye baptized? And they said, Unto John’s baptism.
verses.44019004: Then said Paul, John verily baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying unto the people, that they should believe on him which should come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus.
verses.44019005: When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
verses.44019006: And when Paul had laid his hands upon them, the Holy Ghost came on them; and they spake with tongues, and prophesied.
verses.44019022: So he sent into Macedonia two of them that ministered unto him, Timotheus and Erastus; but he himself stayed in Asia for a season.
verses.44019029: And the whole city was filled with confusion: and having caught Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul’s companions in travel, they rushed with one accord into the theatre.
verses.44020001: And after the uproar was ceased, Paul called unto him the disciples, and embraced them, and departed for to go into Macedonia.
verses.44020004: And there accompanied him into Asia Sopater of Berea; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timotheus; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.
verses.44020006: And we sailed away from Philippi after the days of unleavened bread, and came unto them to Troas in five days; where we abode seven days.
verses.44020015: And we sailed thence, and came the next day over against Chios; and the next day we arrived at Samos, and tarried at Trogyllium; and the next day we came to Miletus.
verses.44020031: Therefore watch, and remember, that by the space of three years I ceased not to warn every one night and day with tears.
verses.44020034: Yea, ye yourselves know, that these hands have ministered unto my necessities, and to them that were with me.
verses.44021004: And finding disciples, we tarried there seven days: who said to Paul through the Spirit, that he should not go up to Jerusalem.
verses.44021008: And the next day we that were of Paul’s company departed, and came unto Cæsarea: and we entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, which was one of the seven; and abode with him.
verses.44021010: And as we tarried there many days, there came down from Judæa a certain prophet, named Agabus.
verses.44021017: And when we were come to Jerusalem, the brethren received us gladly.
verses.44021027: And when the seven days were almost ended, the Jews which were of Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the people, and laid hands on him,
verses.44021028: Crying out, Men of Israel, help: This is the man, that teacheth all men every where against the people, and the law, and this place: and further brought Greeks also into the temple, and hath polluted this holy place.
verses.44021029: (For they had seen before with him in the city Trophimus an Ephesian, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.)
verses.44021030: And all the city was moved, and the people ran together: and they took Paul, and drew him out of the temple: and forthwith the doors were shut.
verses.44021031: And as they went about to kill him, tidings came unto the chief captain of the band, that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.
verses.44021032: Who immediately took soldiers and centurions, and ran down unto them: and when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, they left beating of Paul.
verses.44021033: Then the chief captain came near, and took him, and commanded him to be bound with two chains; and demanded who he was, and what he had done.
verses.44021034: And some cried one thing, some another, among the multitude: and when he could not know the certainty for the tumult, he commanded him to be carried into the castle.
verses.44021035: And when he came upon the stairs, so it was, that he was borne of the soldiers for the violence of the people.
verses.44021036: For the multitude of the people followed after, crying, Away with him.
verses.44021039: But Paul said, I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city: and, I beseech thee, suffer me to speak unto the people.
verses.44022003: I am verily a man which am a Jew, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, and taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers, and was zealous toward God, as ye all are this day.
verses.44022006: And it came to pass, that, as I made my journey, and was come nigh unto Damascus about noon, suddenly there shone from heaven a great light round about me.
verses.44022007: And I fell unto the ground, and heard a voice saying unto me, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?
verses.44022008: And I answered, Who art thou, Lord? And he said unto me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom thou persecutest.
verses.44022009: And they that were with me saw indeed the light, and were afraid; but they heard not the voice of him that spake to me.
verses.44022010: And I said, What shall I do, Lord? And the Lord said unto me, Arise, and go into Damascus; and there it shall be told thee of all things which are appointed for thee to do.
verses.44022017: And it came to pass, that, when I was come again to Jerusalem, even while I prayed in the temple, I was in a trance;
verses.44022018: And saw him saying unto me, Make haste, and get thee quickly out of Jerusalem: for they will not receive thy testimony concerning me.
verses.44022019: And I said, Lord, they know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue them that believed on thee:
verses.44022020: And when the blood of thy martyr Stephen was shed, I also was standing by, and consenting unto his death, and kept the raiment of them that slew him.
verses.44022021: And he said unto me, Depart: for I will send thee far hence unto the Gentiles.
verses.44022025: And as they bound him with thongs, Paul said unto the centurion that stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned?
verses.44022026: When the centurion heard that, he went and told the chief captain, saying, Take heed what thou doest: for this man is a Roman.
verses.44022027: Then the chief captain came, and said unto him, Tell me, art thou a Roman? He said, Yea.
verses.44022028: And the chief captain answered, With a great sum obtained I this freedom. And Paul said, But I was free born.
verses.44023001: And Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men and brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day.
verses.44023006: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men and brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee: of the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question.
verses.44023011: And the night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer, Paul: for as thou hast testified of me in Jerusalem, so must thou bear witness also at Rome.
verses.44023016: And when Paul’s sister’s son heard of their lying in wait, he went and entered into the castle, and told Paul.
verses.44023017: Then Paul called one of the centurions unto him, and said, Bring this young man unto the chief captain: for he hath a certain thing to tell him.
verses.44023018: So he took him, and brought him to the chief captain, and said, Paul the prisoner called me unto him, and prayed me to bring this young man unto thee, who hath something to say unto thee.
verses.44023019: Then the chief captain took him by the hand, and went with him aside privately, and asked him, What is that thou hast to tell me?
verses.44023020: And he said, The Jews have agreed to desire thee that thou wouldest bring down Paul to morrow into the council, as though they would enquire somewhat of him more perfectly.
verses.44023021: But do not thou yield unto them: for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men, which have bound themselves with an oath, that they will neither eat nor drink till they have killed him: and now are they ready, looking for a promise from thee.
verses.44023022: So the chief captain then let the young man depart, and charged him, See thou tell no man that thou hast shewed these things to me.
verses.44023033: Who, when they came to Cæsarea, and delivered the epistle to the governor, presented Paul also before him.
verses.44023035: I will hear thee, said he, when thine accusers are also come. And he commanded him to be kept in Herod’s judgment hall.
verses.44024001: And after five days Ananias the high priest descended with the elders, and with a certain orator named Tertullus, who informed the governor against Paul.
verses.44024027: But after two years Porcius Festus came into Felix’ room: and Felix, willing to shew the Jews a pleasure, left Paul bound.
verses.44025002: Then the high priest and the chief of the Jews informed him against Paul, and besought him,
verses.44025011: For if I be an offender, or have committed any thing worthy of death, I refuse not to die: but if there be none of these things whereof these accuse me, no man may deliver me unto them. I appeal unto Cæsar.
verses.44025012: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, Hast thou appealed unto Cæsar? unto Cæsar shalt thou go.
verses.44026001: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Thou art permitted to speak for thyself. Then Paul stretched forth the hand, and answered for himself:
verses.44026002: I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer for myself this day before thee touching all the things whereof I am accused of the Jews:
verses.44026003: Especially because I know thee to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews: wherefore I beseech thee to hear me patiently.
verses.44026004: My manner of life from my youth, which was at the first among mine own nation at Jerusalem, know all the Jews;
verses.44026005: Which knew me from the beginning, if they would testify, that after the most straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
verses.44026006: And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers:
verses.44026007: Unto which promise our twelve tribes, instantly serving God day and night, hope to come. For which hope’s sake, king Agrippa, I am accused of the Jews.
verses.44026008: Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that God should raise the dead?
verses.44026009: I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
verses.44026010: Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.
verses.44026011: And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.
verses.44026012: Whereupon as I went to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,
verses.44026013: At midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them which journeyed with me.
verses.44026014: And when we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking unto me, and saying in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.
verses.44026015: And I said, Who art thou, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest.
verses.44026016: But rise, and stand upon thy feet: for I have appeared unto thee for this purpose, to make thee a minister and a witness both of these things which thou hast seen, and of those things in the which I will appear unto thee;
verses.44026017: Delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send thee,
verses.44026018: To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.
verses.44027001: And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners unto one named Julius, a centurion of Augustus’ band.
verses.44027002: And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we launched, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia; one Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.
verses.44027003: And the next day we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave him liberty to go unto his friends to refresh himself.
verses.44027004: And when we had launched from thence, we sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
verses.44027005: And when we had sailed over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.
verses.44027006: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us therein.
verses.44027007: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarce were come over against Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, over against Salmone;
verses.44027008: And, hardly passing it, came unto a place which is called The fair havens; nigh whereunto was the city of Lasea.
verses.44027009: Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them,
verses.44027010: And said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage, not only of the lading and ship, but also of our lives.
verses.44027011: Nevertheless the centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship, more than those things which were spoken by Paul.
verses.44027012: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to depart thence also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, and there to winter; which is an haven of Crete, and lieth toward the south west and north west.
verses.44027020: And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.
verses.44028001: And when they were escaped, then they knew that the island was called Melita.
verses.44028003: And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand.
verses.44028016: And when we came to Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard: but Paul was suffered to dwell by himself with a soldier that kept him.
verses.44028030: And Paul dwelt two whole years in his own hired house, and received all that came in unto him,
verses.44028031: Preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, with all confidence, no man forbidding him.
verses.45001001: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, separated unto the gospel of God,
verses.45011001: I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.
verses.45015019: Through mighty signs and wonders, by the power of the Spirit of God; so that from Jerusalem, and round about unto Illyricum, I have fully preached the gospel of Christ.
verses.45015024: Whensoever I take my journey into Spain, I will come to you: for I trust to see you in my journey, and to be brought on my way thitherward by you, if first I be somewhat filled with your company.
verses.45015028: When therefore I have performed this, and have sealed to them this fruit, I will come by you into Spain.
verses.45016007: Salute Andronicus and Junia, my kinsmen, and my fellowprisoners, who are of note among the apostles, who also were in Christ before me.
verses.45016011: Salute Herodion my kinsman. Greet them that be of the household of Narcissus, which are in the Lord.

verses.46001001: Paul, called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and Sosthenes our brother,
verses.46003004: For while one saith, I am of Paul; and another, I am of Apollos; are ye not carnal?
verses.46004012: And labour, working with our own hands: being reviled, we bless; being persecuted, we suffer it:

verses.46015008: And last of all he was seen of me also, as of one born out of due time.

verses.47001001: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy our brother, unto the church of God which is at Corinth, with all the saints which are in all Achaia:
verses.47010001: Now I Paul myself beseech you by the meekness and gentleness of Christ, who in presence am base among you, but being absent am bold toward you:
verses.47011023: Are they ministers of Christ? (I speak as a fool) I am more; in labours more abundant, in stripes above measure, in prisons more frequent, in deaths oft.
verses.47011024: Of the Jews five times received I forty stripes save one.
verses.47011025: Thrice was I beaten with rods, once was I stoned, thrice I suffered shipwreck, a night and a day I have been in the deep;
verses.47011026: In journeyings often, in perils of waters, in perils of robbers, in perils by mine own countrymen, in perils by the heathen, in perils in the city, in perils in the wilderness, in perils in the sea, in perils among false brethren;
verses.47011027: In weariness and painfulness, in watchings often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness.
verses.47011032: In Damascus the governor under Aretas the king kept the city of the Damascenes with a garrison, desirous to apprehend me:
verses.47011033: And through a window in a basket was I let down by the wall, and escaped his hands.
verses.47012007: And lest I should be exalted above measure through the abundance of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me, lest I should be exalted above measure.
verses.47012008: For this thing I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me.
verses.47012009: And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.
verses.48001001: Paul, an apostle, (not of men, neither by man, but by Jesus Christ, and God the Father, who raised him from the dead;)
verses.48001013: For ye have heard of my conversation in time past in the Jews’ religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it:
verses.48001015: But when it pleased God, who separated me from my mother’s womb, and called me by his grace,
verses.48001017: Neither went I up to Jerusalem to them which were apostles before me; but I went into Arabia, and returned again unto Damascus.
verses.48001018: Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to see Peter, and abode with him fifteen days.
verses.48001019: But other of the apostles saw I none, save James the Lord’s brother.
verses.48001020: Now the things which I write unto you, behold, before God, I lie not.
verses.48001021: Afterwards I came into the regions of Syria and Cilicia;
verses.48002001: Then fourteen years after I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, and took Titus with me also.
verses.48002002: And I went up by revelation, and communicated unto them that gospel which I preach among the Gentiles, but privately to them which were of reputation, lest by any means I should run, or had run, in vain.
verses.48002003: But neither Titus, who was with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised:
verses.48002004: And that because of false brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage:
verses.48002005: To whom we gave place by subjection, no, not for an hour; that the truth of the gospel might continue with you.
verses.48002006: But of these who seemed to be somewhat, (whatsoever they were, it maketh no matter to me: God accepteth no man’s person:) for they who seemed to be somewhat in conference added nothing to me:
verses.48002007: But contrariwise, when they saw that the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter;
verses.48002008: (For he that wrought effectually in Peter to the apostleship of the circumcision, the same was mighty in me toward the Gentiles:)
verses.48002009: And when James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars, perceived the grace that was given unto me, they gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship; that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision.
verses.48002010: Only they would that we should remember the poor; the same which I also was forward to do.
verses.48005002: Behold, I Paul say unto you, that if ye be circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing.
verses.49001001: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, to the saints which are at Ephesus, and to the faithful in Christ Jesus:
verses.49003001: For this cause I Paul, the prisoner of Jesus Christ for you Gentiles,
verses.50001001: Paul and Timotheus, the servants of Jesus Christ, to all the saints in Christ Jesus which are at Philippi, with the bishops and deacons:
verses.50001013: So that my bonds in Christ are manifest in all the palace, and in all other places;
verses.50003005: Circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, an Hebrew of the Hebrews; as touching the law, a Pharisee;
verses.50003006: Concerning zeal, persecuting the church; touching the righteousness which is in the law, blameless.
verses.51001001: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timotheus our brother,
verses.51004018: The salutation by the hand of me Paul. Remember my bonds. Grace be with you. Amen.
verses.52001001: Paul, and Silvanus, and Timotheus, unto the church of the Thessalonians which is in God the Father and in the Lord Jesus Christ: Grace be unto you, and peace, from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.52002009: For ye remember, brethren, our labour and travail: for labouring night and day, because we would not be chargeable unto any of you, we preached unto you the gospel of God.
verses.52002018: Wherefore we would have come unto you, even I Paul, once and again; but Satan hindered us.
verses.53001001: Paul, and Silvanus, and Timotheus, unto the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ:
verses.53003017: The salutation of Paul with mine own hand, which is the token in every epistle: so I write.
verses.54001001: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the commandment of God our Saviour, and Lord Jesus Christ, which is our hope;
verses.54001003: As I besought thee to abide still at Ephesus, when I went into Macedonia, that thou mightest charge some that they teach no other doctrine,
verses.55001001: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, according to the promise of life which is in Christ Jesus,
verses.55001008: Be not thou therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner: but be thou partaker of the afflictions of the gospel according to the power of God;
verses.55001017: But, when he was in Rome, he sought me out very diligently, and found me.
verses.55004006: For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand.
verses.55004007: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith:
verses.55004013: The cloke that I left at Troas with Carpus, when thou comest, bring with thee, and the books, but especially the parchments.
verses.55004016: At my first answer no man stood with me, but all men forsook me: I pray God that it may not be laid to their charge.
verses.55004017: Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me; that by me the preaching might be fully known, and that all the Gentiles might hear: and I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion.
verses.55004020: Erastus abode at Corinth: but Trophimus have I left at Miletum sick.
verses.55004022: The Lord Jesus Christ be with thy spirit. Grace be with you. Amen.

verses.56001005: For this cause left I thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city, as I had appointed thee:
verses.56003012: When I shall send Artemas unto thee, or Tychicus, be diligent to come unto me to Nicopolis: for I have determined there to winter.
